authority: syllabus scheme of assessment printed p.36 [PDF 39] and specification grid printed p.37 [PDF 40]; command-word behaviour measured from the papers

ao_code_crosswalk.why: build/make_work_order.py and the checks address AOs by code; these are the syllabus's own A, B and C under build-tool names, not Cambridge AOs

assessment_objectives.name: Knowledge with understanding
assessment_objectives.definition: A1 scientific phenomena, facts, laws, definitions, concepts, theories; A2 scientific vocabulary, terminology, conventions (including symbols, quantities and units); A3 scientific instruments and apparatus, including techniques of operation and aspects of safety; A4 scientific and technological applications with their social, economic and environmental implications.

assessment_objectives.name: Handling information, application and solving problems
assessment_objectives.definition: B1 locate, select, organise and present information from a variety of sources; B2 translate information from one form to another; B3 manipulate numerical and other data B4 use information to identify patterns, report trends and draw inferences; B5 present reasoned explanations of phenomena, patterns and relationships; B6 make predictions and propose hypotheses; B7 solve problems including some of a qualitative nature as they relate to everyday life.

assessment_objectives.name: Practical (experimental and investigative) skills and abilities
assessment_objectives.definition: C1 demonstrate knowledge of how to use apparatus and materials safely (including following a sequence of instructions where appropriate) C2 plan experiments and investigations (including how to record accurate estimates, observations and measurements accurately and make deductions from simple tests) C3 handle and process experimental observations and data (including dealing with anomalous or inconsistent results) C4 apply scientific knowledge and understanding to make interpretations and to draw appropriate conclusions from practical observations and data; C5 evaluate methods and suggest possible improvements

papers_provenance: names, marks and durations printed p.36 [PDF 39]; weightings and AO marks printed p.37 [PDF 40]; ao_split is the AO marks as a share of the paper

ao_mark_budget.stated_basis: STATED by the syllabus: the "Overall Weighting across all components" column of the specification grid, printed p.37 [PDF 40]. It equals the raw marks: A 75, B 45, C 40 of 160. This is the target the AO balance check uses.
ao_mark_budget.final_grade_basis: DERIVED, not stated: each paper's AO marks as a share of that paper, weighted by the stated paper weightings 30/50/20. Recorded for reference; no check balances against it.
ao_mark_budget.recall_ceiling: "not more than 24% recall" inside AO A; denominator undefined (open issue 1)

item_mix_target.note: The stated overall weighting. Balance the SUBJECT against it, never a single topic. Not a card quota.

command_word_rule: used_at_level = observed_count > 0, the repo rule (standard/v0.2.0-draft/mine/assemble.py:144). Words never observed are not used to open prompts; their skills stay in scope.

recall_ceiling.use: not converted into any item count

corpus_totals: Paper 2 contributes 480 marks across its six papers; Paper 3 contributes 240 across its six; together 720 across twelve.

flashcard_subtype_ao_map.tests: A term defined in the syllabus sense
Named parts, features, functions or facts; on a practical objective, the apparatus or reagent
An ordered sequence: a biological process, or the steps of a practical procedure
A full account of a taught multi-step mechanism, every step in order with its cause and effect
The feature that separates two confusable things
The reason for an outcome, a step or a condition
A reasoned explanation of a taught relationship, each link stated (Understand: it reproduces a taught account; applying it to a new case is the APP card)

Taught biology applied to a situation the learner has not met (B7); on a practical objective, knowledge applied to interpret an unfamiliar experiment (C4); also producing a labelled drawing from a specimen or image, and constructing a key
A calculation with working and units
Reading, completing, plotting or concluding from a table, graph or diagram
A source of error or limitation in a method, and an improvement tied to it
A judgement weighed from both sides, for an objective that is itself two-sided
A complete investigation plan: what is changed, measured and kept the same, how, and repeats (devising a procedure)

flashcard_subtype_ao_map_note: The AOs a subtype may carry. Which one a slot carries is set by the explicit proposed demand audit planning/ao_demand_audit.json, applied after the subject-profile base build. Subtype/objective type alone does not determine it.
